title: Pad Thai
subtitle: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, bean sprouts, and tamarind
excerpt: Pad Thai is Thailand's most internationally recognised noodle dish: flat rice noodles stir-fried with egg, bean sprouts, spring onion, and a sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar. The sauce is sweet, sour, and salty in balance. Prawns or chicken are both traditional; tofu works for a vegetarian version.
sourceNotes: Pad Thai was promoted as a national dish of Thailand in the 1930s and 1940s by Prime Minister Plaek Phibunsongkhram as part of a campaign to build national identity. The dish used rice noodles instead of wheat noodles to reduce dependence on Chinese imports. The tamarind-fish sauce-palm sugar base is common across Thai stir-fried dishes. Use a very hot wok for authentic char.

recipe.batchNotes: Cook one or two portions at a time. Stir-frying in volume produces steamed noodles rather than fried.

content.text: Soak the noodles in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking; they should be pliable but not soft. They finish cooking in the wok. The pad Thai sauce (tamarind, fish sauce, sugar) should be mixed and ready before you start cooking, as the stir-fry moves quickly. Do not crowd the wok: cook 2 portions maximum at once.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water 30 minutes, drained
roasted and roughly crushed, to serve

content.text: Mix the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the wok over very high heat until smoking. Add the oil. Stir-fry the garlic for 20 seconds. Add the prawns and cook for 1 minute until pink.
Push everything to one side. Add the drained noodles and pour in the sauce. Toss everything together. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, tossing constantly, until the noodles absorb the sauce.
Push the noodles to one side. Crack the eggs into the empty space. Scramble lightly, then fold into the noodles before fully set.
Add the bean sprouts and spring onion. Toss for 30 seconds. Serve immediately with peanuts, lime wedges, and chilli flakes.

items.cause: Noodles were not sufficiently soaked, or the wok was not hot enough
items.fix: Soak until fully pliable. Use the highest heat your hob allows. Separate the noodles in the pan with tongs before the sauce goes in.
